title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi/parallel tool calls and retries
author: Eleanor Park
description: Context: customers increasingly use multi-tool workflows (e.g., search + executor + external action) and expect predictable streaming behavior, clear injection of tool outputs into the assistant turn, and robust retry semantics when a parallel tool call fails. This PR improves the execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool invocations, tightens behavior of tool result injection (structured output + streaming), and updates the OpenAI-compat layer to preserve backwards-compatible request shapes. Summary of changes: 1) Execution orchestration: introduce a lightweight coordinator that records tool call graph and ensures deterministic injection order for sequential tool calls while allowing parallel execution where safe. The coordinator exposes a per-request timeline used by the streaming layer to interleave assistant tokens and tool outputs. 2) Parallel calls and retries: implement bounded-parallel executor with configurable concurrency per-request, per-tool retry policy, and exponential backoff jitter. Failures and retries now surface as structured tool events rather than raw error strings. 3) Tool result injection: tool outputs are normalized into the structured_output model early; the streaming layer now supports 'tool_delta' events that are compatible with the OpenAI tooling shape (compat note: we add a top-level "tool_event" envelope that older clients will ignore). 4) Streaming stability: add buffering logic to avoid premature end-of-stream when late-arriving tool results are pending; improved backpressure handling between runtime and gateway to prevent interleaving races. 5) OpenAI compatibility: preserve existing fields for openai-compat clients, add opt-in flags to enable structured tool_event envelopes and parallel retry telemetry. 6) Observability: new trace spans for coordinator stages, per-tool retry counters, and metrics for injected result size. 7) Tests and docs: end-to-end integration tests covering multi-tool scenarios, new examples in redwood-examples/tooling, and API docs updates in redwood-docs. Design decisions: - Deterministic injection ordering for sequentially-declared tools avoids surprising assistant restarts. - Parallelism is opt-in per-request via callOptions.concurrency to protect simple single-tool flows. - Retries only apply to idempotent tool annotations or when caller explicitly marks the tool as retryable. - Structured tool events ensure client compatibility while enabling richer UIs. Migration notes: - Default behavior is backward-compatible: if a client does not opt into structured tool_event envelope or concurrency, behavior remains the same. - SDKs (python/ts) are updated in a companion PR to expose callOptions.retryPolicy and callOptions.concurrency; existing call sites will continue to work. Testing: unit tests for coordinator state machine, integration tests simulating slow tools and partial failures, e2e smoke on staging including OpenAI-compat client. Rollout: feature-gated behind runtime flag "tool-calling-exec-v2"; gradual rollout to hosted API + Dedicated for 2 weeks before enabling by default. See release notes and runbook in notes.
commits: feat(tooling): add coordinator state machine and per-request timeline
fix(streaming): buffer streaming end to wait for tool results
chore(docs): add examples and compat notes
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Overall looks great — can we limit default concurrency to 2? Author: set default to 1 in config and added per-request override in sdk (see commit 2).
Priya Shah: Need clearer failure semantics when non-idempotent tool is marked retryable. Author: added explicit error type and validation; SDK will warn at call time.

Daniel Kim: Streaming end-of-stream buffering may increase tail latency; can we add a short timeout? Author: added configurable wait_timeout (default 250ms) and observed negligible tail impact in perf tests.
QA (automated): Integration test failing on flaky e2e; reran CI and the test passed on second run.
Miguel Torres: Approve after nits fixed.
release_notes:
- Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics: deterministic injection ordering, bounded parallelism, and structured tool events.
- Add per-tool retry policies and telemetry.
- Streaming stability improvements to handle late-arriving tool results.
- OpenAI-compat layer preserved; opt-in structured tool_event envelope and per-request concurrency.
- SDK updates (python/ts) add callOptions.retryPolicy and callOptions.concurrency.
merge_outcome_summary: Merged to main via squash. No feature flag regressions found during staged rollout. Runtime flag 'tool-calling-exec-v2' enabled on 10% hosts for 48h then 100% after smoke.
